solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rude books shown after large woman going topless

indicators.note: shown after places the books at the end, following the woman
going topless means the front letter of the large woman's description is dropped

parts.note: large means big
Nora is a woman's name
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a large woman sunbathing topless, with some books on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant can mean ill-mannered or uncouth, a colloquial synonym for rude.

clue.text: Foes routed in melee without any slip-up

indicators.note: a melee is a confused scramble, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Enemies routed in a brawl, with the victors never stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sure-footed moves without stumbling, hence makes no slips or mistakes.

clue.text: On travels Isaac meets Kitty

indicators.note: being on travels means moving about, so these letters wander into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: While abroad, Isaac gets to know a woman called Kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siamese is a breed of pet cat, an example of a kitty in the affectionate sense.

clue.text: One-zero to Indian man

parts.note: a means one
nil means zero

explanation.surface: A one-nil football score in favour of an Indian player.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is a common male given name in India.

clue.text: Horse race

definitions.meaning: the Arabian is a famous breed of horse
a race in the sense of a people

explanation.definitionFit: Arab names both an Arabian horse breed and a Semitic people, two separate dictionary senses.

clue.text: Herculean bride of The Beast

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Beauty and the Beast reimagined: the strongman's wife was really the beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebe, goddess of youth, married Heracles (Hercules) after he was deified.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the deified Heracles took the goddess Hebe as his wife.

clue.text: Jet, silver and uranium in pot

indicators.note: in places silver and uranium inside the pot

parts.note: a jar is a pot or container
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A recipe of jet, silver and uranium stirred together in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like the black stone in a list of materials, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The SEPECAT Jaguar is an Anglo-French jet attack aircraft.

clue.text: Rodent in the open trapped by an American soldier

indicators.note: trapped by means the open-air piece sits inside the soldier pair

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a secret in the open is out

explanation.surface: A rodent out in the open is caught by a US soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An agouti is a burrowing South American rodent related to guinea pigs.

clue.text: Weapon with atomic obliteration near gambling town

indicators.note: obliteration means the atomic letter is wiped out of the combined words

parts.note: taken as written
A stands for atomic, as in A-bomb
Las Vegas is the famous Nevada gambling town

explanation.surface: A weapon of nuclear destruction tested near Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Nevada nuclear tests near Las Vegas, but the weapon is chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas, such as sarin, is a chemical weapon attacking the nervous system.

clue.text: Satirist and writer holding power

indicators.note: holding means the writer surrounds the power letter

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A satirist and an author share the stage, the writer keeping power.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was the great eighteenth-century English satirist of The Dunciad.

clue.text: Numb with melody blasted out in heavy metal? Quite!

indicators.note: blasted out suggests loud music, signalling the letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Ears numbed by a melody blasted out at a heavy metal concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite!' is the setter agreeing that the musical surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Molybdenum is a dense metallic element used in hard steel alloys.

clue.text: Shark in kilos eaten by Chinese statesman

indicators.note: eaten by puts the kilos inside the statesman's name

parts.note: Mao Zedong was the Chinese Communist statesman
K is short for kilos

explanation.surface: A shark weighing many kilos is devoured by Chairman Mao.
explanation.definitionFit: The mako is a fast-swimming species of mackerel shark.

clue.text: Pirate battling English for some treasure?

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island
battling means at war

explanation.surface: A pirate fights the English for a share of the treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverware, such as cups and cutlery, could count as a hoard of treasure.

clue.text: Breather needed, then energy for sudden movement forwards

parts.note: a lung is the organ one breathes with
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A runner needs a breather before a final burst of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, as in fencing.

clue.text: Spiteful gossip once heard to be at odds with authority

parts.note: ex means former, once
a cat is a spiteful, gossiping woman

indicators.note: being at odds means out of agreement, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A former malicious gossip clashes with the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' looks like a homophone signal, but it is anagram fodder making HEDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex cathedra, literally from the chair, means spoken with full official authority, as by the Pope.

clue.text: President dealing with much dirty linen?

parts.note: laundry waiting to be cleaned is the washing
a ton means a large amount, much

explanation.surface: A president embroiled in a scandal, with lots of dirty linen aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirty linen' suggests scandal but means plain laundry; the pieces come in reverse order to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States.

clue.text: No right to begin to copy

indicators.note: No says the right letter is absent from the word for beginning

parts.note: to start is to begin

explanation.surface: Advice that you have no right to begin copying.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat is short for photostat, a photographic copy.

clue.text: Some fancy Nicaean philosopher

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An elaborate thinker from ancient Nicaea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cynics were a school of ancient Greek philosophers such as Diogenes.

clue.text: Secret soldiers at hotel window

parts.note: the SAS is the British army's covert Special Air Service
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Special forces storm in at a hotel window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a sliding window frame, as in a sash window.

clue.text: Go for speed where set point lost

indicators.note: a lost point is gone astray, so the letters are scattered anew

explanation.surface: A tennis player urged to hurry after losing set point.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom urging someone to hurry, to accelerate.

clue.text: Barking setter on chain in elegant shopping location

indicators.note: on places the setter after the chain in this across entry

parts.note: a bond is a chain or fetter

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A barking dog on its lead in a smart shopping district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the dog or the compiler; it is anagram fodder making STREET. Barking is also a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond Street is a fashionable London street of luxury shops.

clue.text: First out in rowing-boat coming to holy place

indicators.note: First out says the opening letter is dropped from the boat's name

parts.note: a coracle is a small round rowing-boat

explanation.surface: The leader of a rowing crew arrives at a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle, like Delphi, was a sacred place where gods were consulted.

clue.text: Assistant cycling back in thought

indicators.note: cycling back sends the front letter round to the end

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant pedalling home, lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion.

clue.text: What cobbler uses very little with no time to spare

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler works on
minute means tiny

explanation.surface: A cobbler using barely anything, in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Last-minute describes something done at the latest possible moment.

clue.text: Cheers, cheers and cheerio

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
ta again means thanks

explanation.surface: A friend's breezy farewell: thanks, thanks, bye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a British informal goodbye, like cheerio.

clue.text: Separate unit for couple linked

definitions.meaning: a single individual article in a list
a pair romantically together, as in 'they are a thing'

explanation.definitionFit: Item means an individual article, and colloquially a couple in a relationship.

clue.text: Employer's part in obvious error

indicators.note: part in signals that the letters are a piece within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of an employer's role lies in a glaring mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs something, an employer in the literal sense.

clue.text: Try skirting length with rosy colour

indicators.note: skirting means going round, so the try goes around the length

parts.note: a go is a try

explanation.surface: Trying on a skirt of the right length gives a rosy glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a warm reddish colour, as in a healthy flush of the cheeks.

clue.text: Sane — completely so!

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone
there and so are both interjections of emphasis, as in there you are

explanation.surface: An emphatic exclamation that someone is perfectly sane.
explanation.definitionFit: All there is an idiom for mentally sound, in full possession of one's faculties.

clue.text: Criminal not caught by IndoEuropean beginner

indicators.note: not means the caught letter is removed from the criminal

parts.note: a crook is a criminal
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
IE is short for Indo-European

explanation.surface: A novice crook evades capture by an Indo-European.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice or new recruit.
